problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $y,$ given by

$$
(q+9)y=-6
$$

where $q$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $q?$

feedback.problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $z,$ given by

$$
-5(p-9)z=10
$$

where $p$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $p?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

Notice that this equation is in the form $az=b.$ In this case, 

$$
a=-5(p-9),\,b=10.
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
-5(p-9)=0.
$$

Solving this for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-5(p-9) & =0 \\ \frac{-5(p-9)}{-5} & =\frac{0}{-5} \\ p-9 & =0 \\ p & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
